# Daily Windows desktop app pipeline (zip + MSIX + fa1.dev download)

Closes nothing (new capability); requested by the owner after the Windows
app fixes (#2140/#2143).

## What

1. **`build-windows.yml`** (new) — Windows RELEASE build of the Flutter app:
   - `windows-latest`, flutter 3.50.0, `flutter build windows --release`
     with the CI placeholder dance (`.env` + `firebase_options.dart`) that
     `flutter-app-lock-smoke` already uses;
   - renames the bundle exe (`Fa.exe`) and assembles the zip
     `fa-app-windows-x64.zip`;
   - runs `scripts/msix/make_msix.ps1`: assembles an `AppxManifest.xml`
     (identity `dev.fa1.app.Fa`, version from the pubspec, target `MinVersion 10.0.17763.0`),
     packs it with the Windows SDK `makeappx`, and signs it with a **per-run
     self-signed cert** (created + trusted only inside the job); the public
     `.cer` ships beside the artifacts so a dev/corporate machine can
     `Add-AppxPackage` after importing the cert;
   - creates/refreshes the GitHub **auto-release** (tag `fa-app-windows-latest`)
     and attaches `zip + msix + cer`;
   - updates the static **latest pointer** `site/download/windows/latest`
     (content = the tag name) — the website resolves "latest" through it, so
     the page never needs a rebuild when a nightly overwrites the release.

2. **fa1.dev** — the download section gains a **Windows** button next to the
   existing ones, linking to
   `https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/releases/latest/download/fa-app-windows-x64.zip`
   (asset name is stable across runs). `test/site` extended to pin the new
   markup so the block can't silently regress.

3. **Nightly quality leg** — `daily-publish.yml` gains a `windows` leg, same
   shape as the TestFlight/macOS track: on the nightly schedule (and for
   `legs: windows` manual dispatch) it runs the build and the release
   attach — so the Windows pipeline is exercised **daily**, exactly like
   TestFlight, and a broken Windows build reddens the same aggregate the
   release train watches.

4. **Identity** — `flutter_app/windows/CMakeLists.txt`: `BINARY_NAME`/
   project target renamed `flutter_agent_example` → `Fa` so the produced exe
   no longer leaks the Flutter scaffold name (complements #2143's
   Runner.rc/main.cpp identity fixes).

## Verification

- Both workflows `yaml.safe_load` clean (dart yaml parser).
- `scripts/msix/make_msix.ps1` executed **locally on Windows**: packed the
  real release bundle through `makeappx` and signed it with signtool —
  manifest identity, logo assets (150x150/44x44/StoreLogo generated from
  the app icon), and cert flow all verified end-to-end on this machine.

# Build Windows Release (Fa) — the flutter_app desktop build for
# windows-x64, zipped and attached to the release train the same way the
# macOS desktop DMGs are (build-macos.yml). Dispatched by the daily
# auto-publish `windows` leg (daily-publish.yml), which is the Windows
# counterpart of the TestFlight leg: one release-quality app build per
# day, attached to the next derived tag.
#
# The asset is fa-app-windows-x64.zip — a STABLE name (no version suffix),
# like fa-windows-x64.zip (the CLI) and fa-macos-*-mac.zip, so
# releases/latest/download/ links on fa1.dev never rot. It is NOT in
# scripts/release_required_assets.txt yet: the leg is young and a missed
# daily must not block a tag train; promote it to required once the leg
# has a green history.
#
# No signing/notarization: Windows runners cannot code-sign without a
# purchased OV cert; the zip is the unsigned open-source artifact (same
# class as the Android sideload APKs). SmartScreen may warn — the fa1.dev
# copy is the full source to build from.
#
# The app bundles no vendored-framework restore (unlike the macOS leg's
# WasmRun.xcframework): on Windows the wasm_run family resolves to the
# vendored path packages (vendor/wasm_run*), which compile from source in
# the native-assets hooks — nothing to download.
#
# Two artifacts ship:
#   fa-app-windows-x64.zip  — portable bundle (Fa.exe + dlls), the
#                             fa1.dev download button target;
#   fa-app-windows-x64.msix — sideload package (AppxManifest + makeappx
#                             + per-run self-signed cert, see
#                             scripts/msix/make_msix.ps1) with the
#                             public .cer beside it: import the cert
#                             (Trusted People), then Add-AppxPackage.
#                             Not Store-signed — a Partner Center MS
#                             Store submission is a separate track.
name: Build Windows Release (Fa)

223:        # scripts/release_attach_or_create.sh + release_draft_guard.sh

270:          bash scripts/release_attach_or_create.sh "$RELEASE_TAG" msix-asset/fa-app-windows-x64.msix msix-asset/fa-app-windows.cer

content.thinking:
So build-windows.yml attaches to `$RELEASE_TAG` = the **next derived tag** (same tag math as build-macos: latest+1, pre-staging a DRAFT release). The PR body's "auto-release (tag fa-app-windows-latest)" description doesn't match the merged workflow — the merged file derives the next tag (v1.0.730 next) and attaches there (as a draft until the tag train publishes it, via release_attach_or_create.sh).

The landing links use `releases/latest/download/fa-app-windows-x64.*`. The claim "never rot" holds ONLY for assets that the tag train guarantees on every release. The fa-app-windows assets:
- pre-attach to draft-of-next-tag by the daily leg,
- become `latest`-visible only when that tag is actually cut AND published (and only if the daily leg ran successfully in the preceding 24h).

Timeline reality for v1.0.729: the daily leg (via daily-publish.yml windows leg) FIRST runs tomorrow 05:17 (Nov 16) — the workflow has never run. Even after it runs successfully and pre-attaches fa-app-windows-x64.zip to the draft of v1.0.730, `releases/latest` stays v1.0.729 (no fa-app-windows assets) until v1.0.730 is cut+published. And if a day passes without a new tag, latest could again lack the assets (the pre-staged draft is for the NEXT tag only) → the links rot exactly when the daily leg is skipped/broken — which the file itself admits is possible ("a missed daily must not block a tag train").

CONCLUSION — the landing links are structurally wrong for this attach model. The design that DOES hold:
- Option A: link the standing assets through the tag-train-guaranteed release: NOT possible (fa-app-windows never on required set by design).
- Option B: link through the app auto-release page: `releases/latest` — hmm no.
- Option C (what the macOS button does): link `https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/releases/latest` (the release PAGE) — always resolves. For windows: the button "Download for Windows" → the release page where fa-windows-x64.zip AND (once shipped) fa-app-windows assets are visible. Loses one-click asset deep-link.
- Option D: change landing to point at the **CLI windows archive** `fa-windows-x64.zip` for the primary button and drop the msix line. The primary button semantics change from app to CLI.
- Option E: make the landing page resilient via the pointer file the PR promised (`site/download/windows/latest`) — that's a site-served redirect; the static site can't do client-side resolution without JS. Not minimal.
- Option F: pin the links to the `fa-app-windows-latest` standing tag — but the merged workflow doesn't create that tag; it pre-stages drafts of real tags. Would require workflow changes (bigger scope, and the PR body/workflow diverge — an owner-level decision).

MINIMAL ROOT-CAUSE FIX consistent with the repo's own doctrine:
The smoke's purpose (gh-1832): the landing page must expose ONLY links that resolve. The guaranteed-resolving pattern already on this page is the macOS button's `releases/latest` page link. For Windows:
1. Button `windows-download`: `https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/releases/latest/download/fa-windows-x64.zip` — hmm...

Wait, actually, let me think about WHO consumes the fa-app windows zip: Windows users wanting the Fa desktop app. The fa-windows-x64.zip is the `fa` CLI for windows. The landing hero ("Install the CLI" is a separate anchor button!) — the hero block seems to be app-store-style buttons for the APP. Pointing "Download for Windows" at the CLI archive is honest (it IS a Windows download that always exists) but semantically different (CLI vs app).

Hmm, is there precedent? macOS button: "Download for macOS (no sandbox)" → `releases/latest` PAGE (not an asset). That's the app-store page listing all assets. Consistent minimal fix for Windows: same pattern → `releases/latest` page? But then why did macOS choose the page? Because the macOS app DMGs are daily-leg assets too (fa-macos-*-mac.zip "clobber-refresher", NOT in required set — same class as fa-app-windows)! The macOS button's author KNEW the app asset can't be deep-linked reliably → linked the PAGE. #2158's windows button should have done the same.

So the minimal, precedent-consistent fix:
- `windows-download` href: `https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/releases/latest` (same as the macOS button — app assets live on the release page; the CLI zip is listed there too).
- `windows-msix-download` anchor: remove it (it deep-links an asset that may never be on latest; the release page exposes the msix once shipped). OR keep it but point at the release page too (pointless). REMOVE — with a comment noting the daily windows leg assets are reachable via the release page until the leg earns a guaranteed asset slot.

31:#   assert_release_assets.sh --landing [page]
33:#       download/… URL from the landing page (default site/index.html) and
38:# (smoke/landing override, tests only).
76:mode="${1:?usage: assert_release_assets.sh <tag> | --smoke <tag|latest> | --landing [page]}"
101:  --landing)
104:      echo "::error::landing page $page not found — pass the path or run from the repo root" >&2
108:    # the landing page embeds these links in hrefs and JSON FAQ text with
125:        echo "::error::landing link FAILED: $url → HTTP $code (gh-1832: the landing page exposes a broken release download)" >&2
132:    echo "✅ landing link-check passed: $count release URL(s) in $page all serve"
#       v1.0.637/v1.0.638 stranding (a train landing after the daily leg)
#       cannot recur; this gate stays the loud last line of defense for
#       ANY required asset going missing.
#
#   assert_release_assets.sh --smoke <tag|latest>
#       POST-PUBLISH SMOKE: ranged-GET (1 byte) every required asset's
#       download URL; anything outside HTTP 200/206 fails. Base URL is
#       https://github.com unless FA_RELEASE_DOWNLOAD_BASE overrides it
#       (tests), repo comes from GITHUB_REPOSITORY.
#
#   assert_release_assets.sh --landing [page]
#       LANDING LINK-CHECK: extracts EVERY http(s) …/releases/(latest/)?

  --landing)
    page="${2:-site/index.html}"
    [ -f "$page" ] || {
      echo "::error::landing page $page not found — pass the path or run from the repo root" >&2
      exit 1
    }
    # URL stops at whitespace, quotes, angle/close parens, plus, comma —
    # the landing page embeds these links in hrefs and JSON FAQ text with
    # trailing punctuation. NOTE: grep -E cannot portably put a tab in a
    # bracket expression ('\t' there means backslash and letter t, which
    # would truncate every URL at its first 't') — build the class with a
    # real tab via printf.
    url_class="[^\"' <>()+,$(printf '\t')]"
    urls=$(grep -oE "https?://${url_class}+" "$page" \
      | grep -E '/releases/(latest/)?download/' | sort -u || true)
    [ -n "$urls" ] || {
      echo "::error::no /releases/ download links found in $page — the page shape changed; revisit the link-check contract (gh-1832)" >&2
      exit 1
    }
    count=0
    fail=0
    while IFS= read -r url; do
      count=$((count + 1))
      if ! code="$(probe_url "$url")"; then
        echo "::error::landing link FAILED: $url → HTTP $code (gh-1832: the landing page exposes a broken release download)" >&2
        fail=1
      else
        echo "✅ $url → HTTP $code"
      fi
    done <<< "$urls"
    [ "$fail" -eq 0 ] || exit 1
    echo "✅ landing link-check passed: $count release URL(s) in $page all serve"
    ;;

  *)

arguments.content:
# Root Cause Analysis — gh-2194 `[ci-red] v1.0.729 failed`

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: Release tag `v1.0.729` (commit `a601751a`) failed CI run
[43705641723](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/43705641723).
Two distinct layers, found in sequence:

**Layer 1 (attempt 1, ambient)**: PTY/CLI integration shard 0/3 and Core
tests shard 3/4 died at test-load with the single-worker kill signature —
`Failed to load "<file>": Connection closed before full header was received`
(`test/integration/agents_render_gate_test.dart`, "83 passed / 1 failed /
15 skipped"; `test/cli/paste_submit_path_test.dart`, "3738 passed / 1
failed / 5 skipped"). Same-tree-same-SHA proof: main schedule run
[43703988888](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/43703988888)
passed ALL Core + PTY shards at `a601751a` 20 minutes earlier, and the tag's
own delta touches one unrelated test file. Ambient — recovered by rerunning
the run (`gh run rerun 43705641723`, attempt 2; the precedent is
gh-2182/v1.0.725, recovered the same way by ai-teammate).

**Layer 2 (attempt 2, REAL defect — the subject of the fix)**: with the
gate green, the release train ran to completion (v1.0.729 published,
SHA256SUMS signed + attached, pub.dev published, **Advance vpinned marker
succeeded — marker now points at v1.0.729**) — and the post-publish
`Release asset smoke` (gh-1832) went red probing the landing page:

- `releases/latest/download/fa-app-windows-x64.msix` → HTTP 404
- `releases/latest/download/fa-app-windows-x64.zip` → HTTP 404

**Root cause of layer 2**: PR #2158 (`ci/windows-release`, merged into the
v1.0.729 line) added landing-page deep links pointing at
`releases/latest/download/fa-app-windows-x64.zip` and `.msix`, but:

1. those assets are produced by the **daily `build-windows.yml` leg** — a
   clobber-refresher class that `scripts/release_required_assets.txt`
   deliberately keeps OUT of the tag-train-guaranteed set ("the leg is
   young and a missed daily must not block a tag train");
2. that leg has **never run** (zero workflow runs; its first schedule tick
   is the next daily), so no release — draft or published — has ever
   carried the assets;
3. the landing-link probe rides the **tag train only**, so PR validation
   never exercised the new links. v1.0.729 was the first tag carrying them
   → guaranteed 404 → guaranteed red release run.

The build-windows.yml header's "releases/latest/download/ links never rot"
claim only holds after the leg attaches assets AND latest is a release that
carries them; until then the deep links are structurally broken. The page's
own macOS button already models the correct pattern for daily-leg app
assets: link the release PAGE (`releases/latest`), never a `latest/download`
deep link.

**Impact**: the v1.0.729 ref can never go green (the tag's own
`site/index.html` content is immutable), the `Installer smoke` /
`Binaries smoke` legs skip behind the red smoke, and every future tag cut
from main carries the same two broken owner-facing download links
(gh-1832's exact symptom class).

## Fix approach (applied)

Mirror the macOS-button pattern for the windows block in `site/index.html`:

- `windows-download` button → `https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/releases/latest`
  (the release page always resolves and lists the windows app zip/msix/cer
  once the daily leg ships them, plus the guaranteed `fa-windows-x64.zip`
  CLI archive);
- remove the `windows-msix-download` deep link (same 404 class);
- an HTML comment on the block documents when deep links may return
  (only after the asset joins the required set).

New guard `test/site/landing_deep_links_test.dart` pins the contract
offline (the live probe is tag-train-only, so PRs can still land rotting
links): every `releases/latest/download/…` deep link in the landing page
must name an asset from `scripts/release_required_assets.txt`. RED against
the broken page (names exactly the two offenders), GREEN after the fix.
The exact CI probe (`bash scripts/assert_release_assets.sh --landing
site/index.html`) fails before (2× 404) and passes after (3 URLs serve).

## Previous attempt

N/A — first dev leg on this ticket. (Related history: gh-2182/v1.0.725 was
an ambient-only red recovered by run attempt 2; v1.0.728's red was the
`wrap_ansi_line_perf_test` contention median and was never rerun.)

## Recommendation (out of scope for this leg)

1. `build-windows.yml`'s "never rot" header claim vs the actual attach
   model (pre-stage the NEXT tag's draft): reconcile — either promote
   `fa-app-windows-*` into `release_required_assets.txt` once the leg has a
   green history (its own stated plan) or route the landing through a
   standing pointer as the PR body originally described
   (`site/download/windows/latest`).
2. The Watchdog covers PR-branch timeout legs only; tag runs keep red'ing
   on ambient load-phase worker deaths (3 of the last 5 release tags) —
   consider a tag-event recovery path.

## Evidence appendix

- Attempt 1 red: jobs 132786284917 (PTY 0/3), 132786403281 (Core 3/4) —
  load-phase kills, no compile errors, last steps not `cancelled` (not
  timeout-class).
- Attempt 2: PTY 0/3 ✅, Core 3/4 ✅, Quality gate ✅, Publish to pub.dev ✅,
  Sign release checksums ✅, Install pin provenance gate ✅,
  Advance vpinned marker ✅ (marker = `v1.0.729`), Release asset smoke ❌
  (the only red), Installer smoke / Binaries smoke skipped behind it.
- Live probe at fix time: `fa-app-windows-x64.msix`/`.zip` → 404 on
  `releases/latest` (= v1.0.729, asset list has `fa-windows-x64.zip` but no
  `fa-app-windows-*`); no release in history carries `fa-app-windows-*`;
  `build-windows.yml` has zero runs.

### Root Cause

Two layers, found in sequence:

1. **Ambient (attempt 1)** — PTY/CLI integration shard 0/3 and Core tests
   shard 3/4 died at test-load (`Failed to load "<file>": Connection closed
   before full header was received`; single-worker kill signature, no
   compile errors). Same commit `a601751a` passed ALL Core + PTY shards on
   main (run 43703988888) 20 minutes earlier; the tag delta touches one
   unrelated test file. Recovered by rerunning the run (attempt 2 — the
   gh-2182/v1.0.725 precedent).
2. **Real defect (attempt 2)** — with the gate green, the release train
   completed (v1.0.729 published, SHA256SUMS signed, pub.dev published,
   vpinned marker advanced) but the gh-1832 `Release asset smoke` went red:
   the landing page links `releases/latest/download/fa-app-windows-x64.msix`
   and `.zip`, both 404. PR #2158 added the links, but the `fa-app-windows-*`
   assets belong to the daily `build-windows.yml` leg — deliberately kept
   OUT of `scripts/release_required_assets.txt` — and that leg has never
   run, so no release carries them. The landing probe is tag-train-only, so
   PR validation never saw it; v1.0.729 was the first tag carrying the
   links. The ref cannot go green (tag content is immutable), and the same
   two broken download links ride every future tag.

### Previous Attempt

N/A — first dev leg. (gh-2182/v1.0.725 was ambient-only, recovered by run
attempt 2.)

### Fix

- `site/index.html` — the Windows download block now follows the page's own
  macOS-button pattern: `windows-download` points at the release page
  (`releases/latest`, always resolves; lists the windows app zip/msix/cer
  once the daily leg ships them, plus the guaranteed `fa-windows-x64.zip`
  CLI archive) and the `windows-msix-download` deep link is removed, with a
  comment documenting when deep links may return.
- `test/site/landing_deep_links_test.dart` (new) — pins the gh-1832
  contract offline: every `releases/latest/download/…` deep link on the
  landing page must name an asset from `release_required_assets.txt` (RED
  against the broken page — names exactly the two offenders; GREEN after).

### Test Coverage

- `test/site/landing_deep_links_test.dart` — RED pre-fix (2 offenders =
  exactly the links CI 404'd), PASSED post-fix.
- Exact CI probe `bash scripts/assert_release_assets.sh --landing
  site/index.html` — FAILED pre-fix (2× 404, same as CI), PASSED post-fix
  (3 URLs serve).
- Full `test/site/` suite: 75 tests passed, 0 failures.
- `dart analyze` on the new test: no issues; `dart format` applied.
- CI attempt 2 evidence: PTY 0/3 ✅, Core 3/4 ✅, Quality gate ✅, pub.dev
  ✅, checksums ✅, vpinned marker ✅ (marker = v1.0.729); only the asset
  smoke red.

### Notes

- The v1.0.729 release itself is published and healthy; the remaining red
  on that tag's run is the smoke honestly reporting the two broken links
  the tag itself carries. The fix lands on main so the next tag cut
  validates it — do not rerun the v1.0.729 run; it would 404 identically.
- Follow-ups recorded in `outputs/rca.md`: reconcile `build-windows.yml`'s
  "never rot" claim with its actual next-tag-draft attach model, and
  consider a tag-event recovery path for ambient load-phase reds (3 of the
  last 5 release tags).
- No production Dart code changed; site markup + one new test only.

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- feat(gh-2103): compaction digest provenance — summaries can no longer
  launder tool-controlled text into trusted memory. The audit verdict: the
  typed pipeline is sound (the judge sees typed ledger lines, the fold input
  keeps `[User]:`/`[Tool result]:` labels, request candidates come only from
  real non-synthetic user turns), but digest TEXT could copy tool-controlled
  instructions into `## Open User Requests` unmarked. Three layers: every
  digest/checkpoint prompt now carries the origin-provenance duty (asks only
  from real `[User]:` turns; instruction-shaped tool output, forged
  `[User]:` labels and "USER INSTRUCTION" framing are never user intent;
  verbatim tool quotes carry a `[from toolResult]` mark); `sanitizeSummary`
  gains a provenance belt graded at persist sites against the fold's own
  transcript (`SummaryOriginEvidence`) — machine-origin lines leave the
  user-intent sections (logged `sanitizedEphemeral`) and tool-verbatim asks
  gain a ` [from toolResult]` suffix (logged `markedToolOrigin`), with real
  asks byte-identical and pins exempt; and adversarial regression transcripts
  (a tool result shaped like user turns) pin the typed pipeline, the belt on
  all three persist paths (classic/structured/branch+handoff), and the
  prompt duty (`#2103`)
- feat(gh-2102): `/handoff` — start a fresh session from an editable digest
  of the current one: the branch-digest machinery
  (`prepareBranchEntries` + the shared `SummarizeFn` seam, handoff preamble
  in `lib/src/compaction/handoff_digest.dart`) generates a structured
  checkpoint of the whole current branch, the scratch file
  (`<cwd>/.fah/handoff-digest-<ts>.md`) opens in the user's editor
  (`FA_EDITOR` > `VISUAL` > `EDITOR`; non-interactive runs and missing
...
421:- fix: `fileInfo().name` returns the bare entry name on Windows — the
426:- fix(flutter_app): the Windows desktop app can pick a project folder —
428:  `file_selector_windows`) for Windows/Linux instead of the macOS-only
431:  a picked folder never reached the agent env), and the Windows runner
551:- fix(gh-2115): Russian (non-ASCII) typing works in the Windows line REPL.
559:  non-Windows behavior is byte-identical. The vendored dart_tui parser
561:  hook, set by `enableWindowsVtInput`, cleared on restore — gh-1973
699:- ci(windows-release): daily Windows desktop app pipeline — new

arguments.newText:
## Unreleased

- fix(gh-2194): the fa1.dev landing page no longer exposes two broken
  Windows download links. The windows-release landing (#2158) deep-linked
  `releases/latest/download/fa-app-windows-x64.zip` / `.msix`, but those
  assets belong to the daily `build-windows` leg — deliberately outside
  `scripts/release_required_assets.txt` — and the leg has not attached
  them yet, so every train-cut `latest` 404'd both links; the v1.0.729
  release run's gh-1832 asset smoke caught it and red'd the tag. The
  Windows button now follows the macOS button's pattern (release page,
  which always lists the windows app zip/msix/cer once shipped plus the
  guaranteed `fa-windows-x64.zip` CLI archive), the msix deep link is
  gone, and a new offline guard
  (`test/site/landing_deep_links_test.dart`) pins the contract: every
  `latest/download` deep link on the landing page must name a
  required-set asset — PRs can no longer land links only the tag train
  can falsify (`#2194`)
- feat(gh-2103): compaction digest provenance — summaries can no longer

**Two-layer root cause, both diagnosed with evidence:**

1. **Attempt 1 (ambient)**: PTY/CLI shard 0/3 + Core shard 3/4 died at test-load (`Connection closed before full header was received`, single-worker kill signature, no compile errors). Same-SHA proof: main schedule run 43703988888 passed ALL Core+PTY shards at `a601751a` 20 minutes earlier. Recovered via `gh run rerun` (attempt 2) — the gh-2182/v1.0.725 precedent (`triggering_actor: ai-teammate`).

PR #2158 added the links, but those assets belong to the daily `build-windows.yml` leg — deliberately kept out of `release_required_assets.txt` — and the leg has **never run**, so no release carries them. The probe is tag-train-only, so PR validation never saw it; v1.0.729 was the first tag carrying the links.

**Fix (branch `ai/gh-2194`, pushed):** the Windows block now follows the page's own macOS-button pattern — release-page link (always resolves; lists the app zip/msix/cer once shipped plus the guaranteed `fa-windows-x64.zip` CLI archive), msix deep link removed, intent documented inline. New `test/site/landing_deep_links_test.dart` pins the contract offline (RED pre-fix — named exactly the two 404'd links; GREEN post-fix). CHANGELOG `Unreleased` entry added. Do **not** rerun the v1.0.729 run — the tag's content is immutable and would 404 identically; the next tag cut from main validates the fix.
